Define additive, dominance and epistatic QTL effects calibrated to targets

Source: R/define_genome_effects.R
define_genome_effects.Rd

Selects QTL from a filtered genome_meta table, samples additive, dominance and additive-by-additive (A x A) effects, and calibrates them so that the stored targets G_A, G_D and G_AA are delivered exactly under a named anchor. Writes them under the reserved effect owner "generated", replacing the traits' whole generated model. The non-additive sibling of define_additive_effects(): the same pipe subject, target rules, base resolution and owner.

Use define_additive_effects() for line-scoped or parent-of-origin additive models (crossbreeding variants); use this function when dominance or epistasis may be part of the model. With an additive-only target the two write identical rows for the same seed.

Usage

define_genome_effects(
  tbl,
  trait_name,
  G_A = NULL,
  G_D = NULL,
  G_AA = NULL,
  trait_var_comp_tbl = NULL,
  pairs = NULL,
  n_pairs = NULL,
  anchor = c("genic", "realised"),
  dominance_degree_mean = 0.19,
  dominance_degree_sd = 0.097,
  inbreeding_depression = NULL,
  base_tbl = NULL,
  warn_bounds = c(0.8, 1.25),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

tbl

A tidybreed_table from get_table()("genome_meta"), optionally filtered with dplyr::filter(). Every selected locus is a QTL of every trait in the call (one shared QTL set), and A x A pairs are drawn or checked within it.

trait_name

Character vector of existing traits (from define_trait()). With two or more, the architectures are drawn jointly and each target is a k x k matrix across them; the call calibrates the traits together, so a stored block that pairs one of them with a trait outside the call is refused.

G_A, G_D, G_AA

Optional targets for the additive, dominance and additive_by_additive blocks: a symmetric positive-semidefinite k x k matrix with dimnames in trait_name order (or unnamed, taken in that order), or a single number when there is one trait. A passed block is written to trait_var_comp with the effects, and is refused if that block is already stored for any of the traits. NULL (default) reads the block from storage, and leaves it out of the model when none is stored. An additive block is required; see Targets.

trait_var_comp_tbl

Optional filtered get_table(pop, "trait_var_comp"): the stored rows to use for the blocks not passed, e.g. filter(effect_name != "dominance") to leave a stored dominance target out of this model. NULL (default) reads the stored population-wide rows.

pairs

Optional data frame with columns locus_name_1 and locus_name_2: your own A x A design, one row per interacting pair of selected loci. Needs an additive_by_additive target; not with n_pairs. See Pairs.

n_pairs

Optional whole number, 1 to floor(m / 2) for m selected loci: how many random disjoint pairs to draw. NULL (default, with pairs = NULL) pairs every QTL once. Needs an additive_by_additive target.

anchor

"genic" (default) or "realised": the reference population the targets are exact for. See Details.

dominance_degree_mean, dominance_degree_sd

Shape of the dominance architecture: each QTL's dominance effect is drawn as d = h |a|, with degree h ~ N(mean, sd) and a its sampled additive effect, before calibration rescales the dominance effects to G_D. A positive mean makes most heterozygotes better than the homozygote average, so the model has inbreeding depression. Defaults 0.19 and 0.097. Used only with a non-zero dominance target; both 0 is refused.

inbreeding_depression

Optional numeric vector named by trait, e.g. c(ADG = 1.2): the drop in the trait mean per unit of inbreeding F (positive = depression) to build in. For each named trait it replaces dominance_degree_mean with the value that delivers it; traits not named keep dominance_degree_mean. Needs a non-zero dominance target and dominance_degree_sd > 0. See Inbreeding depression.

base_tbl

Optional tidybreed_table from get_table() (optionally filtered) whose allele frequencies are the base: the founder pool (founder_haplotypes), allele copies (ind_haplotype) or individuals (any table with id_ind). The base frequencies centre the effects and set the genic anchor. NULL (default) uses the whole founder table. Required under anchor = "realised", where it must select individuals.

warn_bounds

c(lower, upper) with 0 < lower <= upper: after calibration the delivered blocks are compared with another population's view (see Details), and a ratio outside the bounds warns. Default c(0.8, 1.25); NULL turns the comparison off.

seed

Optional integer, applied with set.seed() immediately before the draw, after every input check and after each block's anchor feasibility check, so those refusals never touch the RNG. A failure that depends on the draw itself – the drawn architecture's rank, the additive floor, or a calibration that fails verification – comes after the seed and has consumed RNG draws. NULL (default) draws from the current stream, so a preceding set.seed() reproduces the call too.

Value

The tidybreed_pop, invisibly. The effects are written to the genome_effects tables under the owner "generated", and any passed target to trait_var_comp. Run add_tgv() to evaluate them.

Details

The model. In functional coding the genotypic value is g = sum_j a_j (x_j - 1) + sum_j d_j 1[x_j = 1] + sum_(k,l) e_kl (x_k - 1)(x_l - 1), x the dosage of allele 1. Its exact statistical (NOIA) re-expression has additive effects alpha_j = a_j + b_j d_j + sum_l e_jl c_l (c_l = 2 p_l - 1), dominance effects d and A x A effects e. The three targets are covariances of those three components.

When the result is exact. Every present block (G_A, and G_D / G_AA when present) is delivered under the named anchor to a relative tolerance of 1e-8 on the correlation scale. That is checked, never assumed: a calibration that misses it is an error before anything is written.

How. Highest order first: the A x A architecture is calibrated to G_AA; the dominance architecture, d = h |a| with dominance degrees h ~ N(dominance_degree_mean, dominance_degree_sd), is calibrated to G_D; then, with the coupling b d + sum e c the first two induce now fixed, the additive architecture is solved so the statistical additive effects deliver G_A. Each stage is a k x k right factor of its drawn architecture, so the same seed gives the same architecture.

The additive floor. Dominance and epistasis already induce additive variance (b d and e c are part of alpha). Part of it the additive architecture can cancel, part it cannot; G_A below what it cannot cancel is refused, and the error names that minimum per trait. The floor belongs to the sampled architecture, not to G_D / G_AA alone: another seed gives another floor, and with every base frequency at 0.5 under "genic" it is zero however large G_D is.

The anchor is the reference covariance the calibration is exact for:

  • "genic" (default): the random-mating (HWE + linkage-equilibrium) limit at the base allele frequencies. Use it for multi-generation studies.

  • "realised": the covariances of the individuals base_tbl selects, linkage disequilibrium included. extract_genetic_variance()(anchor = "realised") on the same individuals gives each target block back. The blocks need not be uncorrelated in that cohort, so its total variance also carries a between_components covariance. The effects are still stored with HWE-referenced contrasts centred at the base frequencies, so the stored additive / dominance components of ind_tgv are not the cohort's own split; each individual's total genetic value is the same either way. base_tbl must select individuals with complete genotypes, and the in-memory design arrays have a size limit.

Under linkage disequilibrium the additive component of a realised cohort is a contrast component, not a joint regression: calibration is exact for the anchor and nothing more.

After calibration the delivered blocks are compared with what another population sees: the genic limit under "realised"; the base individuals' own covariances under "genic" when base_tbl selects individuals; the founder pool's expectation of the additive block only (dominance and A x A would need the pool's multi-locus LD). A departure outside warn_bounds warns (the pool comparison is a message). Nothing is stored.

Targets

Each block (additive, dominance, additive_by_additive) comes from exactly one source:

  • a passed matrix (G_A, G_D, G_AA; a number for one trait), written to trait_var_comp in the same transaction as the effects. It is refused when that block is already stored for any of the traits, even as an identical matrix, and whether or not trait_var_comp_tbl shows it;

  • otherwise the rows of trait_var_comp_tbl (a filtered get_table(pop, "trait_var_comp")), or, when it is NULL, the stored population-wide rows.

A block that comes from neither is absent from the model; a zero matrix is an explicit exact zero, and writes no terms. An additive block is required. A model with no non-zero dominance or A x A block takes the additive-only route: the same draw, calibration and rows as define_additive_effects(). To add a block later, store or pass it and re-run: the additive architecture draw is unchanged by the new block (same seed).

Non-zero dominance or A x A targets need a positive-definite G_A: this release solves the additive stage for a full-rank factor. A correlation of +/-1 or a zero additive variance is accepted for additive-only models. Singular targets are reported with a message, since a typed 1 meant as 0.99 looks the same.

Pairs

A x A acts on pairs of QTL, used only with an additive_by_additive block:

  • pairs, a data frame locus_name_1, locus_name_2: your design. A locus may appear in several pairs (a hub gene); unknown loci, loci outside the filter, self-pairs and repeated pairs (in either order) are errors.

  • pairs = NULL: a random matching, each QTL in at most one pair, as AlphaSimR does. n_pairs = NULL pairs every QTL once (floor(m / 2) pairs), and a message says so.

Within a pair the loci are ordered by name (C locale), and pairs are written sorted by locus id, so the stored order does not depend on the draw.

Crossbreeding and scope

Effects are common to every line (no line_name or parent_origin; line or parent-specific non-additive effects are a later release). Common effects still give heterosis, through allele-frequency differences between lines. The default base pools the founder table, so the targets then hold at the pooled frequencies (with a Wahlund warning); pass base_tbl to calibrate on one reference line.

What a re-run replaces

Every "generated" term of the traits, at every scope: line-scoped additive variants from define_additive_effects() included (the message counts them). Terms of other owners are untouched. Afterwards define_additive_effects() refuses these traits while their generated model has dominance or A x A terms; re-run this function with an additive-only target, or use remove_generated_effects().

Generated means calibrated

There is no option to write fixed or unscaled effects. Exact coefficients go through define_genome_effect_terms() with ad_terms() / aa_terms() under a user owner, for example:

pop |>
  define_genome_effect_terms(
    trait_name = "ADG",
    terms = rbind(
      ad_terms(locus_name = c("Locus_10", "Locus_44"),
               a = c(0.30, -0.12), d = c(0.10, 0.05), p = c(0.35, 0.60),
               coding = "functional"),
      aa_terms(locus_name_1 = "Locus_10", locus_name_2 = "Locus_44",
               e = 0.08, p_1 = 0.35, p_2 = 0.60, coding = "functional")))

Inbreeding depression

inbreeding_depression (the drop in the mean per unit of inbreeding F, positive = depression, sum 2pq d) sets each named trait's mean dominance degree. It is exact for one trait. With several traits each requested trait's mean is solved as if it stood alone, and the joint calibration then mixes the columns, so the delivered depression is approximate, with no closeness guarantee; a message gives requested and delivered values. It is not stored.

See also

define_additive_effects() for line-specific or imprinted additive effects; extract_genetic_variance() to measure what a population has; define_effect_cov_matrix() to store a target first; define_genome_effect_terms(), ad_terms() and aa_terms() for known coefficients; remove_generated_effects().

Examples

# A small in-memory population
set.seed(1)
pop <- open_pop(pop_name = "dge_example", db_name = ":memory:") |>
  define_genome(n_loci = 200, n_chr = 2, chr_len_Mb = 100) |>
  define_founder_haplotypes(n_haplotypes = 200)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmplKq43k/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Opened in-memory population 'dge_example'
#> Defined genome: 200 loci across 2 chromosomes | chr lengths (Mb): all equal to 100 Mb
#>   Tables written: genome_meta, genome_map, ind_haplotype, ind_genotype, ind_crossover, chr_inheritance, chr_recombination, genome_effects, genome_effect_members, genome_effect_member_origins
#>   Views created: genome_effect_terms, genome_effect_loci
#> Generating 200 founder haplotypes (method = "uniform")...
#>   Created founder_haplotypes (200 haplotypes x 200 loci)
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("founder_haplotypes") |>
  add_founders(n_males = 50, n_females = 50, line_name = "A")
#> Added 100 founders (50 males, 50 females) to line 'A'
for (t in c("ADG", "BF", "WW", "LS", "FI", "IMF")) pop <- define_trait(pop, t)
#> Added trait 'ADG'.
#> Added trait 'BF'.
#> Added trait 'WW'.
#> Added trait 'LS'.
#> Added trait 'FI'.
#> Added trait 'IMF'.

# Additive, dominance and A x A targets for one trait, QTL on chromosome 1.
# The targets are written to trait_var_comp with the effects; the A x A
# pairs are a random matching of the QTL.
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("genome_meta") |>
  dplyr::filter(chr_name == "1") |>
  define_genome_effects("ADG", G_A = 0.3, G_D = 0.1, G_AA = 0.05,
    seed = 21)
#> Drew 50 random A x A pairs: every QTL paired once (floor(100 / 2)), as AlphaSimR does. Pass n_pairs for fewer pairs, or pairs for a chosen design (a locus may then appear in several pairs).
#> Set genome effects for 100 QTL and 50 pairs on trait ADG (base: founder_haplotypes): exact under the genic anchor; delivered additive variance 0.3; dominance variance 0.1; additive-by-additive variance 0.05.
#> Additive floor for this sampled architecture (the least additive variance its dominance and A x A effects allow; another draw gives another floor): ADG = 0.1266. G_A - floor has smallest eigenvalue 0.578 on the correlation scale.
#> Inbreeding depression (drop in the mean per unit of F, positive = depression; sum 2pq d under the genic anchor's frequencies): implied ADG = 2.233.
#> Functional effects (sampling: dominance_degree_mean = 0.19, dominance_degree_sd = 0.097): ADG: 100 QTL with a != 0, 100 with d != 0, 50 pairs with e != 0.
#> The founder pool (pool expectation under random pairing; additive block only, dominance and additive-by-additive not compared) sees relative spectrum [0.892, 0.892] of the target (sampling LD of 200 haplotypes).

# Measure it: the genic anchor at the founder frequencies gives the
# targets back
pop |>
  get_table("ind_meta") |>
  extract_genetic_variance(trait_name = "ADG", anchor = "genic",
    base_tbl = get_table(pop, "founder_haplotypes"))
#> Genic (HWE + linkage equilibrium) expectation at the allele frequencies of 'founder_haplotypes', an explicit base (allele copies).
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   effect_name     trait_name_1 trait_name_2 cov_value n_ind decomposition anchor
#>   <chr>           <chr>        <chr>            <dbl> <int> <chr>         <chr> 
#> 1 additive        ADG          ADG              0.3     100 full          genic 
#> 2 dominance       ADG          ADG              0.100   100 full          genic 
#> 3 additive_by_ad… ADG          ADG              0.05    100 full          genic 
#> 4 total           ADG          ADG              0.45    100 full          genic 

# Two correlated traits with dominance, and an inbreeding depression for
# BF (approximate with several traits: a message gives the delivered value)
G_A <- matrix(c(0.3, 0.1, 0.1, 0.4), 2, 2)
G_D <- diag(c(0.08, 0.05))
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("genome_meta") |>
  define_genome_effects(c("BF", "WW"), G_A = G_A, G_D = G_D,
    inbreeding_depression = c(BF = 1.5), seed = 22)
#> Set genome effects for 200 QTL on traits BF, WW (base: founder_haplotypes): exact under the genic anchor; delivered additive [BF,BF = 0.3; BF,WW = 0.1; WW,WW = 0.4]; dominance [BF,BF = 0.08; BF,WW = -1.43077e-17; WW,WW = 0.05].
#> Additive floor for this sampled architecture (the least additive variance its dominance and A x A effects allow; another draw gives another floor): BF = 0.02238, WW = 0.01478. G_A - floor has smallest eigenvalue 0.658 on the correlation scale.
#> Inbreeding depression (drop in the mean per unit of F, positive = depression; sum 2pq d under the genic anchor's frequencies): BF requested 1.5, delivered 1.18895. Approximate for several traits: each requested trait's degree mean is solved as if it stood alone and the joint calibration mixes the columns, so there is no closeness guarantee.
#> Functional effects (sampling: dominance_degree_mean = 0.19, dominance_degree_sd = 0.097; solved degree mean BF = 0.0574576): BF: 200 QTL with a != 0, 200 with d != 0; WW: 200 QTL with a != 0, 200 with d != 0.
#> The founder pool (pool expectation under random pairing; additive block only, dominance and additive-by-additive not compared) sees relative spectrum [0.923, 1.02] of the target (sampling LD of 200 haplotypes).

# Your own A x A design: one hub locus interacting with three others
pairs <- data.frame(locus_name_1 = "Locus_10",
                    locus_name_2 = c("Locus_20", "Locus_30", "Locus_40"))
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("genome_meta") |>
  dplyr::filter(chr_name == "1") |>
  define_genome_effects("LS", G_A = 0.2, G_AA = 0.05, pairs = pairs,
    seed = 23)
#> Set genome effects for 100 QTL and 3 pairs on trait LS (base: founder_haplotypes): exact under the genic anchor; delivered additive variance 0.2; additive-by-additive variance 0.05.
#> Additive floor for this sampled architecture (the least additive variance its dominance and A x A effects allow; another draw gives another floor): LS = 0.09074. G_A - floor has smallest eigenvalue 0.5463 on the correlation scale.
#> Functional effects (sampling: dominance_degree_mean = 0.19, dominance_degree_sd = 0.097): LS: 100 QTL with a != 0, 3 pairs with e != 0.
#> The founder pool (pool expectation under random pairing; additive block only, dominance and additive-by-additive not compared) sees relative spectrum [0.988, 0.988] of the target (sampling LD of 200 haplotypes).

# Additive only first, dominance added later. The stored G_A is read back,
# and with the same seed the additive architecture draw is unchanged.
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("genome_meta") |>
  define_genome_effects("FI", G_A = 1, seed = 24)
#> Set genome effects for 200 QTL on trait FI (base: founder_haplotypes): exact under the genic anchor; delivered additive variance 1.
#> The founder pool (pool expectation under random pairing) sees relative spectrum [1.12, 1.12] of the target (sampling LD of 200 haplotypes).
pop <- pop |> define_effect_cov_matrix("dominance", 0.2, trait_name = "FI")
#> Stored 'dominance' covariance matrix for: FI.
pop <- pop |> get_table("genome_meta") |> define_genome_effects("FI", seed = 24)
#> Replaced 200 generated terms of trait 'FI'.
#> Set genome effects for 200 QTL on trait FI (base: founder_haplotypes): exact under the genic anchor; delivered additive variance 1; dominance variance 0.2.
#> Additive floor for this sampled architecture (the least additive variance its dominance and A x A effects allow; another draw gives another floor): FI = 0.08266. G_A - floor has smallest eigenvalue 0.9173 on the correlation scale.
#> Inbreeding depression (drop in the mean per unit of F, positive = depression; sum 2pq d under the genic anchor's frequencies): implied FI = 3.95.
#> Functional effects (sampling: dominance_degree_mean = 0.19, dominance_degree_sd = 0.097): FI: 200 QTL with a != 0, 200 with d != 0.
#> The founder pool (pool expectation under random pairing; additive block only, dominance and additive-by-additive not compared) sees relative spectrum [1.11, 1.11] of the target (sampling LD of 200 haplotypes).

# Exact in the founders themselves, linkage disequilibrium included
pop <- pop |>
  get_table("genome_meta") |>
  dplyr::filter(chr_name == "2") |>
  define_genome_effects("IMF", G_A = 0.2, G_D = 0.05, anchor = "realised",
    base_tbl = get_table(pop, "ind_meta"), seed = 25)
#> Set genome effects for 100 QTL on trait IMF (base: ind_meta): exact under the realised anchor; delivered additive variance 0.2; dominance variance 0.05.
#> Additive floor for this sampled architecture (the least additive variance its dominance and A x A effects allow; another draw gives another floor): IMF = 0.01428. G_A - floor has smallest eigenvalue 0.9286 on the correlation scale.
#> Inbreeding depression (drop in the mean per unit of F, positive = depression; sum 2pq d under the realised anchor's frequencies): implied IMF = 1.484.
#> Functional effects (sampling: dominance_degree_mean = 0.19, dominance_degree_sd = 0.097): IMF: 100 QTL with a != 0, 100 with d != 0.
pop |>
  get_table("ind_meta") |>
  extract_genetic_variance(trait_name = "IMF")
#> Realised genetic covariances of the 100 selected individuals (frequencies and regressions are the cohort's own).
#> # A tibble: 4 × 7
#>   effect_name     trait_name_1 trait_name_2 cov_value n_ind decomposition anchor
#>   <chr>           <chr>        <chr>            <dbl> <int> <chr>         <chr> 
#> 1 additive        IMF          IMF             0.2      100 full          reali…
#> 2 dominance       IMF          IMF             0.05     100 full          reali…
#> 3 between_compon… IMF          IMF            -0.0156   100 full          reali…
#> 4 total           IMF          IMF             0.234    100 full          reali…

# Evaluate the genetic values
pop <- pop |> get_table("ind_meta") |> add_tgv(c("ADG", "IMF"))
#> Computed TGV for 100 individuals on trait 'ADG' (additive, dominance, interaction).
#> Computed TGV for 100 individuals on trait 'IMF' (additive, dominance).
close_pop(pop)
